ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
To depict an electrostatic field, equipotential lines can be used. The interference fringes in thin-film interference are essentially lines of equal thickness, meaning that the thickness of the film is the same at every point along the same interference fringe. When using the setup shown in the figure to check for flatness, the shape of the interference fringes observed can determine the locations of depressions or protrusions on the surface being tested. When the wavelength of the monochromatic light source is λ.

1. What is the thickness difference of the film at the centers of two adjacent bright fringes?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: To depict an electrostatic field, equipotential lines can be used. The interference fringes in thin-film interference are essentially lines of equal thickness, meaning that the thickness of the film is the same at every point along the same interference fringe. When using the setup shown in the figure to check for flatness, the shape of the observed interference fringes can determine the locations of depressions or protrusions on the surface being tested. When the wavelength of the monochromatic light source is λ, what is the thickness difference of the film at the centers of two adjacent bright fringes?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the monochromatic light labeled "Monochromatic light" is incident from above onto the transparent "Template"; below there is "Slice/Checked plane"; a very thin gap film is formed between the template and the checked plane; the interference fringes correspond to positions where the film thickness is the same. Reasoning: The same fringe involves two beams of light reflected from the upper and lower boundaries of the film, and the variable optical path difference caused by the film thickness t is 2t. The centers of adjacent bright fringes are adjacent interference maxima, and the optical path difference differs by one wavelength, namely Δ(2t)=λ. Therefore 2Δt=λ, obtaining that the film thickness difference at the centers of adjacent bright fringes is Δt=λ/2.
